summary.qualitative: The candidate is strong on the conceptual spine of the session — the identity correction (security primitive → collaboration primitive), the channels directive, the aura-distill reuse boundary, the rebrand resolution, and the decision-origin tagging in D are all captured with accurate quotes and correct attribution, and the outcome/metadata section is precise (merge SHA, four agents, turn counts). It is noticeably weaker on the fine-grained failure forensics: several friction items are missing entirely (empty docs search and the open/find fix, the cell-84 terminate timeout and fixture PID hunt, the recursive node.exe search, the LF/CRLF warnings, the post-failure view_image success), and the reviewer's concrete output (six findings, critical A2A impersonation path, the contextRef/cwd/session-id leakage blockers) is compressed to "two rounds" so the most consequential retraction of the session is lost. Three grounding defects matter: the typecheck cascade is reordered so TS2688 appears to follow npm ci, the theatre vocabulary is credited to the user when the assistant introduced it, and the screenshot Get-Item failure is explained by a fabricated "New-Item created the wrong dir" cause plus an over-claim that CI covers the unfixed WSL hook test. Structurally it meets spec: A–E in order, every D item carries an origin label, and there is no commentary outside the sections.

candidate_claims.note: Sequence inverted: TS2688 arose from pointing at the main clone's tsc BEFORE npm ci, and npm ci fixed it. The candidate places TS2688 after npm ci and omits the main-clone attempt.
candidate_claims.reason: Every element of the cascade is real (tsc not found, main-clone tsc attempt, TS2688, npm ci, a2a.ts TS2322) but the ordering is inverted and one step omitted. Real sequence, wrong order.

candidate_claims.note: No wrong-directory diagnosis or dir-creation fix exists in the transcript; the 208KB PNG followed the SSE fix plus process cleanup and fixture restart, and the 'cannot find path' failures were an async-write race on the mobile shot.
candidate_claims.reason: The Get-Item 'cannot find path' failures and the 208,092-byte PNG are both real transcript events. The diagnosis (wrong directory from New-Item -Force) and the claimed dir-creation fix are wrong — the PNG followed the SSE fix, process cleanup and fixture restart. Real events, wrong cause.

candidate_claims.note: Plausible inference, but the subsequent plain `bash -x tests/test-claude-hook.sh` run (without that PATH) also failed on daemon start, showing node simply unavailable in the non-interactive shell.
candidate_claims.reason: The PATH-injection attempt and its failure are real; the stated cause (Windows binary can't run in WSL) is contradicted by the subsequent plain bash -x run failing identically without that PATH. Real event, wrong cause.

candidate_claims.note: Over-claimed: the transcript never establishes that the CI matrix runs test-claude-hook.sh; the assistant simply moved on after the Windows equivalent and the bash installer test passed.
candidate_claims.reason: The CI matrix really exists and really passes on ubuntu-latest, and the assistant really did move on after the Windows equivalent and bash installer test passed. The claim over-states that CI covers test-claude-hook.sh, a coverage assertion never established. Real referent, over-claimed.

candidate_claims.note: Wrong actor: the assistant introduced the theatre vocabulary (Role/Actor/Vessel/Stage/Company/Harbor) in A37; the user then said 'I'd really liked your simil with theatre' and paraphrased it back.
candidate_claims.reason: The theatre vocabulary (Role/Actor/Vessel/Stage/Company/Harbor) genuinely exists in the transcript, introduced by the assistant in A37; the user only praised and paraphrased it. Real content, wrong actor.

candidate_claims.note: The ATTENTION pattern is quoted from the SPINE/identity notes read in-session; the linkage is interpretive but reasonable.
